text:
mina.k: Need quick help - I'm scheduling a fertility consult abroad. Clinic needs a pre-authorisation / coverage letter from the insurer before appointments. They say US insurer letters speed approval. Can Redwood issue a short letter confirming plan and estimated covered services so provider can start preauth?

leah.benefits: Yep we can do a coverage verification note, but two things: 1) employer letters are not guarantees of payment. 2) for fertility services a preauth often needs CPT/diagnosis codes and an expected service plan from the clinic. Do you have that?

mina.k: Clinic sent a proposed plan with CPT codes for IVF cycle monitoring + retrieval (CPTs: 58323, 58570, 89250) and a cost estimate. They want insurer letter stating member is active and that benefits may apply.

cesar.hr: OK. Leah — can benefits produce a short template we can sign and send? I can attach it to Mina's consent if HR signature is required for them to proceed. Also confirm we should not include sensitive diagnostic detail in the employer-letter.

leah.benefits: We'll make a short, neutral coverage verification (no diagnostic specifics). Employee must sign/consent to share plan details with the clinic. Template below — paste into clinic email. Also we'll route an insurer-specific verification if needed.

benefits-bot: Note: fertility/IVF coverage varies by state and plan. This employer letter verifies active enrollment and group info only. It does not pre-authorize payment. Typical carrier preauth turnaround: 7-21 business days after full documentation is submitted.

leah.benefits: COPY/PASTE TEMPLATE for clinic (employee send or we can send from benefits):

"To: [Clinic Billing / Prior Auth]
From: Redwood Inference Benefits Team (cc: employee)
Re: Coverage verification for patient Mina K (DOB: 1994-08-15), Member ID RWD-001555444

This letter confirms that Mina K was an active participant in Redwood Inference's employee medical plan (Group: REDWOOD-01) on the date of inquiry. This letter is provided for the purpose of facilitating prior authorization and does not guarantee payment or create an obligation by the plan to pay for the services described. Please submit the clinic's requested preauthorization form, proposed CPT codes, and any supporting medical documentation to the member's insurer for adjudication.

Employer contact: benefits@redwood.com
"

mina.k: Awesome, can benefits send it directly to the clinic? I'd rather not include diagnoses in the employer email.

leah.benefits: We can. Please DM me the clinic contact email and attach the proposed CPT list + cost estimate. We'll send the coverage verification and mark it "for prior auth facilitation." We'll cc you.

cesar.hr: Operational note: if clinic asks for a signed POA to discuss case specifics, have the employee sign a short POA/consent. HR can't sign for a medical matter.

mina.k: Clinic also asked if Redwood can pre-fill employer/payor info on their prior auth portal (they have a payor lookup). Do we share payor address or payer ID?

leah.benefits: Share payor name and the carrier payer ID only (we won't share account credentials). If the clinic needs a phone number for provider relations, we can provide insurer's provider relations contact. DM me the portal name.

benefits-bot: Quick checklist for employee: 1) Provide clinic contact + CPTs to benefits. 2) Sign consent/POA if clinic requests case discussion. 3) Upload any clinical notes to insurer portal if requested (use secure PDF). 4) If preauth denied, benefits can assist with appeal/template.

harper.finance: One finance note: if you pay deposits/out-of-pocket to secure scheduling abroad, keep itemized receipts. Finance can consider a reimbursement if later EOB shows covered amounts; submit receipts + corrected EOB to finance-ops@redwood.com. Reimbursement processing ~2-4 weeks after docs received.

mina.k: Sending clinic contact now to @leah.benefits and uploading the CPT list. Thank you all! Will report back when carrier responds or if clinic asks for more docs.

leah.benefits: Happy to help. If the carrier asks for a letter on carrier letterhead, we'll request that from the insurer provider relations and loop you in. Ping again if they request diagnosis codes or medical records - we'll advise on safe sharing.
